meta.description: Habitat and science stops chosen by the team from data/candidate_sites.json. Names, briefings, photos and facts are NASA text and images; 'task' is null because no NASA source gives one.

habitat.name: Habitat (Perseverance landing site)
habitat.note: Start of Perseverance's earliest drive (sol 14) in NASA's traverse data. NASA calls the landing site 'Octavia E. Butler'.

stops.name: Séítah
stops.briefing: The first close-up look at the oldest rocks in Jezero crater visited by Perseverance happened in this spot. Dubbed the Séítah formation, these rocks revealed a geologic story that no one had anticipated.

photo.title: Perseverance Rover's View of South Séítah
photo.description: Composed of 84 enhanced-color images [...] the mosaic was taken on Sept. 12, 2021 (the 201st Martian day, or sol, of the mission), by the Mastcam-Z imager as the rover was parked on an elevated overlook just outside its entry point into South Séítah.
photo.note: Resized to at most 2400 px wide by the team; not cropped or edited.

stops.name: Delta front
stops.briefing: After years of anticipation starting with compelling views from orbit, Perseverance arrived at the front of the ancient delta deposit that motivated the selection of Jezero crater for the Mars 2020 mission. Mastcam-Z responded with the biggest panorama yet taken.

photo.title: Perseverance Explores the Jezero Crater Delta
photo.description: Those images were acquired on June 12, 13, 16, 17, and 20, 2022 (the 466th, 467th, 470th, 471st, and 474th Martian day, or sol, of Perseverance's mission).
photo.note: Resized to at most 2400 px wide by the team; not cropped or edited.

stops.name: Belva crater
stops.briefing: After traversing much of the Jezero delta fan deposit, Perseverance stopped to peer into its largest crater, called Belva, to get a look into the third dimension of the deposit, revealing details of its stratigraphy.

photo.title: Perseverance Takes in View at Belva Crater
photo.description: This view of the interior of Belva Crater was generated using data collected by the Mastcam-Z instrument aboard NASA's Perseverance Mars rover on April 22, 2023, the 772nd Martian day, or sol, of the mission. When the 152 individual images that make up this mosaic were taken, the rover was parked at the west side of the crater's rim, on a light-toned rocky outcrop the science team is calling “Echo Creek.”
photo.note: Resized to at most 2400 px wide by the team; not cropped or edited.
